intro: Zambia, once Northern Rhodesia, is a peaceful country built on copper and known for its wildlife and Victoria Falls.

chapters.title: Early peoples
text: The 'Broken Hill skull', found at Kabwe, belonged to an early human relative who lived about 300,000 years ago. Bantu-speaking peoples later formed kingdoms such as the Lozi and the Bemba.

chapters.title: Northern Rhodesia
text: David Livingstone explored the region in the 1850s. Rhodes's company took control, and copper mining on the Copperbelt began in the 1920s.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Zambia became independent in 1964 under Kenneth Kaunda, who led until 1991. It supported liberation movements in neighbouring countries. Power has changed hands peacefully several times.

highlight.title: Peaceful
highlight.text: Zambia has never had a civil war.
